column1: # Anchor set -- transcribed from "Known_Opioid_Peptides_v11.xlsx" sheet
# 'Anchor set (20)' (2026-10-26), then extended and corrected against the
# primary papers (2026-10-27). Anchors 21-26 were added from Chiba 1989 Table 1,
# which the v11 sheet drew on but did not exhaust.
# FREE ACIDS ONLY. Per 'Removed from order' Filter 1 and the user's instruction
# 2026-10-27: plain sequence, no amides, esters, D-residues or non-natural
# residues. That filter is what excludes DAMGO and deltorphin-II from Block A
# and both casoxin methyl esters from Block C, and it is why `native` and
# `cofold_seq` differ for #1 and #18.
# AFFINITIES ARE NOT POOLED ACROSS BLOCKS. One block = one document = one assay.
#   A  Wang 2023 Cell 186:413-427 Table S2 -- pKi, radioligand, HEK293T, one lab
#   B  Koch 1985 Naunyn-Schmiedeberg's 331:351-354 Table 2 -- KD uM, rat brain
#   C  Chiba, Tani & Yoshikawa 1989 J Dairy Res 56:363-366 Table 1
#   D  Tani 1990 Agric Biol Chem 54:1803 Table 1 -- IC50 uM
# mu_affinity IS THE COLUMN TO CORRELATE AGAINST, and it is a single measure per
# block: pKi (A, carried in mu_pKi), KD (B), binding IC50 (C, D). A '/' means
# the source reports two preparations and both are kept. '>' is a censored lower
# bound, ranked at the bound and never treated as a measurement.
# mu_A2_uM IS NOT AN AFFINITY and is never correlated against. Chiba reports a
# GPI A2 -- the concentration that doubles DAGO's IC50 -- alongside the binding
# IC50, and the v11 sheet labelled some A2 values as IC50. The two disagree in
# rank: YPSYG is the strongest binder in the table (42 uM) but a weak functional
# antagonist (A2 500 uM), while SYPYY is a weak binder (700 uM) and the
# strongest functional antagonist (A2 16 uM). Co-folding confidence is a
# structural quantity, so the binding IC50 is the right target; the A2 is here
# for interpretation only.
